Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test expects
  - The objective is f(x) = (1 − x)^2 with bounds [-1e6, 0.5]. The true minimizer (x = 1) is outside the upper bound, so the optimizer must return the clipped upper bound x = 0.5. The test asserts result[0] <= 0.5.

- How CMAESOptimizer handles bounds
  - The optimizer works in an “encoded” space when bounds are present: FitnessFunction.encode maps actual x to a unit interval [0,1] per coordinate, and decode maps back:
    - encode: res[i] = (x[i] − lower[i]) / (upper[i] − lower[i]) (lines 904–913).
    - decode: res[i] = (upper[i] − lower[i]) * x[i] + lower[i] (lines 929–937).
  - With the test’s bounds, the encoded location of the true minimizer x = 1 is > 1: (1 − (−1e6)) / (0.5 − (−1e6)) ≈ 1.0000005.
  - Therefore, if the search is not constrained to [0,1], the algorithm will push the encoded mean beyond 1 to pursue lower objective values, which decodes to x > 0.5 (i.e., out of bounds).

- Where enforcement fails
  1) Offspring feasibility checking is effectively disabled by default.
     - In doOptimize’s generation loop (lines 374–389), a candidate arxk is generated and a check is performed only up to checkFeasableCount times:
       - Loop condition: for (i = 0; i < checkFeasableCount + 1; i++) { ... if (i >= checkFeasableCount || fitfun.isFeasible(...)) break; ... }.
       - With the default constructor, DEFAULT_CHECKFEASABLECOUNT is used, and checkFeasableCount = 0.
       - Consequently, i starts at 0, the condition i >= checkFeasableCount is immediately true (0 >= 0), so the loop breaks without ever calling isFeasible. No feasibility check is performed; offspring outside [0,1] are accepted and evaluated.
  2) Returned point is not repaired to bounds.
     - When updating the best solution, the returned point is constructed with:
       optimum = new PointValuePair(fitfun.repairAndDecode(bestArx.getColumn(0)), ...)
       (lines 418–421).
     - FitnessFunction.repairAndDecode simply calls decode(x) (lines 920–923) and does not perform any repair/clipping despite isRepairMode being set to true by default (lines 895–898).
     - Thus, even if a candidate is out of the encoded [0,1] range, decoding will produce actual values outside [lower, upper], and those out-of-bounds values are returned to the caller.

- Why the test fails
  - Starting from x = 0, the encoded start is very close to 1. The algorithm, unconstrained in the encoded space, can and will explore values > 1 to move towards the true minimizer x = 1. Because no feasibility check is performed (checkFeasableCount = 0), and repairAndDecode does not enforce bounds, the best decoded point can be > 0.5 and is returned as-is. The test then observes result[0] > upper[0], causing the assertion failure.

- Summary
  - Two combined issues lead to “CMAESOptimizer does not enforce bounds”:
    1) With the default settings, feasibility checks are effectively disabled in the generation loop (checkFeasableCount = 0), so offspring can be out-of-bounds in encoded space.
    2) Even at the point of returning the best solution, repairAndDecode does not clip/repair to the feasible region; it merely decodes linearly, propagating out-of-bounds encoded points into out-of-bounds actual points.
  - This matches the reported bug: The optimizer can exceed user-specified bounds and return out-of-bounds solutions.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
